questions.questionText: Which of the following is the fundamental purpose of planning?

options.content: helping the organization reach its objectives

questions.explanation: According to the contemporary view of planning, its fundamental purpose is to help the organization achieve its goals.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 160: "The fundamental purpose of planning, however, is to help the organization reach its objectives."

questions.questionText: The primary management function is
questions.explanation: Planning is explicitly defined as the primary management function that serves as the foundation for organizing, influencing, and controlling.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 161: "Planning is the primary management function—the one that precedes and is the basis for the organizing, influencing, and controlling functions."

questions.questionText: The main disadvantage of arriving at decisions through consensus is

options.content: it results in very few practical solutions
it reduces employees' commitment to the decision
often the manager must make the decision
it focuses "several heads" on the decision

questions.explanation: The main disadvantage explicitly stated in the textbook for consensus-based decision making is that it involves time-consuming discussions relating to the decision. Features like focusing 'several heads' and boosting employee commitment are listed as advantages.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 185: "The main disadvantage of this method is that it often involves time-consuming discussions relating to the decision, which can be costly to the organization."

questions.questionText: _________ is the assignment of various portions of a particular task among a number of organization members.
questions.explanation: Division of labor is defined explicitly as the assignment of various portions of a particular task among a number of organization members to increase specialization and efficiency.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 252: "Division of labor is the assignment of various portions of a particular task among a number of organization members."

questions.questionText: _________ is the process of sharing information with other individuals.
questions.explanation: Communication is explicitly defined in the textbook as the process of sharing information with other individuals.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 348: "Communication is the process of sharing information with other individuals."

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of planning?
questions.explanation: One of the key advantages of planning is that it enhances decision coordination across the organization by focusing managers on the future and overarching objectives.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 162: "Advantages of planning include... it enhances decision coordination; and it emphasizes organizational objectives."

questions.questionText: Formal groups are commonly divided into
questions.explanation: The slides explicitly divide Formal Groups into two kinds: 'Command Group' and 'Task Group'. Interest and friendship groups are types of informal groups.
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 9.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is one of the characteristics of a group as used in management-related discussions?

options.content: A group is simply a gathering of people.
Groups always work toward the accomplishment of an organizational goal.
A group must consist of 5 or more people.
Groups are characterized by occasional communication among members over time.
A group consists of members who are psychologically aware of one another.

questions.explanation: In management context, a group is more than just a gathering of people. It is any number of people who interact, are psychologically aware of one another, and perceive themselves to be a group. Note that informal groups do not always work toward organizational goals.
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 4.

questions.questionText: _________ is managerial activity aimed at bringing organizational performance up to the level of performance standards.
questions.explanation: Corrective action is the specific managerial activity in the controlling process aimed at correcting mistakes and bringing organizational performance up to the level of the established performance standards.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 506: "Corrective action is managerial activity aimed at bringing organizational performance up to the level of performance standards."

questions.questionText: _________ is the systematic effort to compare performance to predetermined standards in order to determine whether performance is in line with those standards, or needs to be corrected.
questions.explanation: Roberto Mockler's formal definition of controlling explicitly states it is a systematic effort by business management to compare performance to predetermined standards to determine whether performance is in line with those standards.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 502: "According to Roberto Mockler, controlling is a systematic effort by business management to compare performance to predetermined standards, plans, or objectives to determine whether performance is in line with these standards..."

questions.questionText: Of the four primary management functions, organizing usually precedes planning.
questions.explanation: According to the 'Primacy of Planning' concept, planning is the foundational function that must occur before all others. It provides the basis for organizing, influencing, and controlling. Thus, organizing does not precede planning; planning precedes organizing.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 161: "Planning is the primary management function—the one that precedes and is the basis for the organizing, influencing, and controlling functions."

questions.questionText: In the nominal group technique, group members never meet face to face.
questions.explanation: In the Nominal Group Technique, members present ideas orally, write them on a board for all to see, and discuss them simultaneously, which requires meeting face to face. It is the Delphi Technique that gathers ideas from members who are geographically separated and do not meet face to face.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 195: "In contrast to the nominal group technique or brainstorming, the Delphi technique does not have group members meet face to face."

questions.questionText: Implementation of the chosen alternative is the final step in the decision-making process.
questions.explanation: According to the rational decision-making process model, implementing the chosen alternative is the fourth step. The fifth and final step is gathering problem-related feedback to determine the effect of the implemented alternative on the identified problem.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 187: Figure 8.3 shows Step 4 is 'Implement chosen alternative' and Step 5 is 'Gather problem-related feedback.'

questions.questionText: Bureaucracy can be characterized as a management system with detailed procedures, rules, and a clearly outlined organizational hierarchy with impersonal relationships among organization members.
questions.explanation: Max Weber's concept of bureaucracy is precisely defined by these exact characteristics. It is a system intended to increase organizational efficiency through strict adherence to rules, formal hierarchies, and impersonal interactions.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 252: "Bureaucracy is the term Max Weber used to describe a management system that includes three primary components: detailed procedures and rules, a clearly outlined organizational hierarchy, and impersonal relationships among organization members."

questions.questionText: Communication is considered a supplementary management skill rather than a fundamental management skill.
questions.explanation: The textbook indicates that chief executives rank communication skills extremely high—tying for first place as the most important skill to teach management students. Thus, it is a fundamental, not supplementary, management skill.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 351: "Table 15.1 shows that chief executives rank communication skills... tying for rank 1 as the most important skill that should be taught to management students."

questions.questionText: A task group is a formal group outlined in the chain of command on an organization chart.
questions.explanation: A command group is defined as the formal group outlined in the chain of command on an organization chart. A task group is a formal group of organization members who interact with one another to accomplish most of the organization's nonroutine tasks.
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 9.

questions.questionText: After actual performance has been measured and compared with established performance standards, the next step in the controlling process is to take corrective action if necessary.
questions.explanation: The three steps of the controlling process are: 1) Measuring performance, 2) Comparing measured performance to standards, and 3) Taking corrective action. Therefore, taking corrective action is the logical next step after comparison if performance deviates from standards.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 506: "After actual performance has been measured and compared with established performance standards, the next step in the controlling process is to take corrective action if necessary."

questions.questionText: In order to preserve their position power, managers should avoid doing personal favors for subordinates.
questions.explanation: Doing personal favors is a strategy to develop a sense of obligation toward the manager, which increases their personal power, not their position power. Position power is derived from the formal organizational position a manager holds, so doing personal favors does not diminish or preserve it.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 508: "To increase personal power, a manager should attempt to develop the following attitudes and beliefs in other organization members: 1. A sense of obligation toward the manager... The basic strategy suggested for creating this sense of obligation is to do personal favors for people."

questions.questionText: Planning involves choosing tasks that must be performed to attain organizational goals, outlining how the tasks must be performed, and indicating when they should be performed.
questions.explanation: The textbook explicitly defines planning as the systematic development of action programs aimed at reaching agreed-upon business objectives, which involves determining the tasks, the methods, and the timeline.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 159: "Planning is the process of determining how the organization can get where it wants to go... choosing tasks that must be performed to attain organizational goals, outlining how the tasks must be performed, and indicating when they should be performed."

questions.questionText: Planning is concerned only with organizational success in the short term, while organizing is concerned with the more distant future (long term).
questions.explanation: Planning encompasses both the short term and the long term. Organizational objectives are typically broken down into short-term, intermediate-term, and long-term targets.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 166: "Organizational objectives can be grouped into three categories: short-term, intermediate-term, and long-term objectives."

questions.questionText: Influencing is the process of assigning the tasks developed under the planning function to various individuals or groups within the organization.
questions.explanation: The statement describes 'Organizing', not 'Influencing'. Organizing is the process of assigning tasks developed under the planning function to various individuals or groups within the organization. Influencing involves guiding the activities of organization members in appropriate directions.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 6: "Organizing can be thought of as assigning the tasks developed under the planning function to various individuals or groups within the organization... Influencing can be defined as guiding the activities of organization members in appropriate directions."

questions.questionText: Organizing is also commonly referred to as motivating, leading, directing, or actuating.
questions.explanation: Motivating, leading, directing, or actuating are all alternative terms used to describe the 'Influencing' function of management, not the 'Organizing' function.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 6: "Influencing is another of the basic functions within the management process. This function—also commonly referred to as motivating, leading, directing, or actuating—is concerned primarily with people..."

questions.questionText: Technical skills involve the ability to apply specialized knowledge and expertise to work-related techniques and procedures.
questions.explanation: According to Robert L. Katz's classic view of management skills, technical skills are explicitly defined as the ability to apply specialized knowledge and expertise to work-related techniques and procedures.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 11: "Technical skills involve the ability to apply specialized knowledge and expertise to work-related techniques and procedures."

questions.questionText: Human skills, unlike technical skills, involve the ability to see the organization as a whole.
questions.explanation: The ability to see the organization as a whole is the definition of 'Conceptual Skills'. 'Human Skills' are defined as the ability to build cooperation and work effectively with people.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 11: "Conceptual skills involve the ability to see the organization as a whole... Human skills build cooperation within the team being led."

questions.questionText: The affirmative purpose of planning is to minimize risk by reducing the uncertainties surrounding business conditions and clarifying the consequences of related management activities.
questions.explanation: Minimizing risk and reducing uncertainties is defined as the 'protective' purpose of planning. The 'affirmative' purpose is to increase the degree of organizational success.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 160: "The protective purpose of planning is to minimize risk by reducing the uncertainties surrounding business conditions... The affirmative purpose is to increase the degree of organizational success."

questions.questionText: Organizations exist for various purposes but have the same types of objectives.
questions.explanation: Because organizations exist for various purposes, their objectives vary significantly based on their unique environment, customers, and operations.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 165: "Organizations exist for various purposes and thus have various types of objectives."

questions.questionText: Suboptimization is the process of assigning subobjectives to the various people or units in the organization based on the organizational objectives.
questions.explanation: Suboptimization occurs when high-level organizational objectives are cascaded and broken down into specific sub-objectives for different departments and units.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 169: "Suboptimization is a condition wherein organizational subobjectives are conflicting or not directly aimed at accomplishing the overall organizational objectives... allocating subobjectives ensures alignment."

questions.questionText: The management by objectives (MBO) approach has been found to be ineffective for nonprofit organizations.
questions.explanation: Management by Objectives (MBO) is a highly applicable strategy across both for-profit and nonprofit organizations because it aligns individual and organizational goals.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 170: "Most managers find MBO programs beneficial. MBO continually emphasizes what should be done in an organization to achieve organizational goals..."

questions.questionText: A decision that is routine and repetitive, and typically handled in a specific way, is frequently called a non-programmed decision.
questions.explanation: Decisions that are routine and repetitive are called programmed decisions. Nonprogrammed decisions, on the other hand, are typically one-shot, ill-structured, or novel policy decisions.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 182: "A programmed decision is routine and repetitive, and the organization typically develops specific ways to handle such decisions."

questions.questionText: Decisions made through consensus usually take up lesser time than those made by a single individual.
questions.explanation: One of the primary disadvantages of consensus or group decision making is that it takes longer. It involves time-consuming discussions for the group to present and consider all members' views before arriving at an agreement.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 185: "The main disadvantage of this method is that it often involves time-consuming discussions relating to the decision, which can be costly to the organization."

questions.questionText: Implementation of the chosen alternative is the final step in the decision-making process.
questions.explanation: Implementation is the fourth step of the rational decision-making process. The final step is gathering problem-related feedback to verify if the alternative actually solved the problem.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 187: "5. Gather feedback to find out whether the implemented alternative is solving the identified problem."

questions.questionText: Groupthink is a group decision-making process in which negative feedback on any suggested alternative by any group member is forbidden until all members have presented alternatives that they perceive as valuable.
questions.explanation: Groupthink is not a structured process where feedback is forbidden; rather, it is a psychological phenomenon where "the desire for agreement so dominates the group that it overrides the need to realistically appraise alternative problem solutions." It results in members censoring their own ideas to conform.
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 16.

questions.questionText: The final step in the organization process is to allocate resources and directives for subtasks.
questions.explanation: Allocating resources and directives for subtasks is Step 4 of the organizing process. The actual fifth and final step is evaluating the results of the organizing strategy to gather feedback and improve the system.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 250 (Figure 11.2): Outlines the organizing process. Step 4 is "Allocate resources and directives for subtasks." Step 5 is "Evaluate results of organizing strategy."

questions.questionText: Span of management refers to the number of organizational levels below that of a particular manager's.
questions.explanation: Span of management (also called span of control) refers to the number of individuals a manager directly supervises, not the number of vertical organizational levels below them.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 262: "Span of management—also called span of control, span of authority, span of supervision, and span of responsibility—is the number of individuals a manager supervises."

questions.questionText: Recruitment is the process of developing qualities in human resources that will enable them to be more productive and thus contribute more to organizational goal attainment.
questions.explanation: The statement provided in the question is the exact textbook definition of 'Training'. Recruitment, on the other hand, is defined as the 'initial attraction and screening of the supply of prospective human resources available to fill a position'.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 303: "Training is the process of developing qualities in human resources that will enable them to be more productive..." compared to Textbook Page 297: "Recruitment is the initial attraction and screening of the supply..."

questions.questionText: Wikstrom's human resource inventory forms are meant to be used exclusively for filling managerial positions and cannot be used for filling nonmanagerial positions.
questions.explanation: While Wikstrom's specific examples (like the Management Inventory Card) focus heavily on management personnel, the textbook explicitly notes that similar forms can be used to keep a human resource inventory of nonmanagerial personnel as well.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 299: "As you can see, Wikstrom’s forms... are focused on management personnel. Of course, similar forms could be used to keep a human resource inventory of nonmanagerial personnel."

questions.questionText: The process of guiding the activities of organization members in appropriate directions is called controlling.
questions.explanation: Guiding the activities of organization members in appropriate directions is the definition of 'Influencing'. Controlling is formally defined as ensuring that an event occurs as it was planned to occur.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 502: "Stated simply, control entails ensuring that an event occurs as it was planned to occur."

questions.questionText: The basic elements of the interpersonal communication process are the source, the encoder, and the decoder.
questions.explanation: The statement is false because it omits the "signal." The three basic elements of the interpersonal communication process are the source/encoder, the signal, and the decoder/destination.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 348: "To be a successful interpersonal communicator, a manager must understand the three basic elements of interpersonal communication: the source/encoder, the signal, and the decoder/destination."

questions.questionText: A task group is a formal group outlined in the chain of command on an organization chart.
questions.explanation: The formal group outlined in the chain of command is a 'Command Group'. A 'Task Group' is formed to accomplish nonroutine tasks.
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 9.

questions.questionText: Measuring performance is the first step in the controlling process.
questions.explanation: The three steps of the controlling process explicitly list 'Measuring performance' as the very first step.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 503: "As Figure 21.2 illustrates, there are three main steps in the controlling process: 1. Measuring performance 2. Comparing measured performance to standards 3. Taking corrective action."

questions.questionText: For control to be successful, all individuals involved in controlling must have a working knowledge of how the control process operates.
questions.explanation: To make controlling successful, managers must ensure the communication of the mechanics of the control process. This means ensuring that all individuals involved in controlling must have a working knowledge of how the process operates.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 509: "The lesson here is simple: For control to be successful, all individuals involved in controlling must have a working knowledge of how the control process operates."

questions.questionText: Most managers have substantial control over increasing their position power.
questions.explanation: Position power is derived strictly from the organizational position a manager holds, which usually depends on promotions that managers have little personal control over. However, managers do have substantial control over increasing their 'personal power' by building relationships.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 508: "Position power is generally enhanced by a move to a higher organizational position, but most managers have little personal control over when they will move up in an organization. Managers do, however, have substantial control over the amount of personal power they hold over other organization members."

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of planning?
questions.explanation: Enhancing decision coordination is explicitly listed as a core advantage of the planning function because it aligns the decision-making of different managers.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 162: "A second advantage of planning is that it enhances decision coordination."

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an error managers make during the controlling stage of management?

options.content: not taking the time to communicate properly with organization members
not monitoring progress in carrying out plans
not exploring enough viable alternatives for reaching objectives

questions.explanation: Controlling involves monitoring and measuring performance to ensure events occur as planned. Therefore, failing to monitor the progress of carrying out those plans is a direct error in the controlling stage. (Establishing departments is Organizing; communication is Influencing; alternatives are Planning).
questions.reference: Textbook Page 502: "...managers should continually control—that is, check to see that organizational activities and processes are going as planned."

questions.questionText: The more resources unused during the production process, the more ________ the manager.
questions.explanation: Managerial efficiency refers to the proportion of total organizational resources that contribute to productivity. Therefore, the textbook explicitly states that if more resources are unused or wasted, the manager is considered inefficient.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 10: "The more resources wasted or unused during the production process, the more inefficient is the manager."

questions.questionText: A manager is considered efficient and effective if the manager

options.content: does not reach goals and does not waste resources
reaches goals and does not waste resources
does not reach goals and wastes resources

questions.explanation: Effectiveness is defined as making substantial progress toward organizational goals ('doing the right things' or reaching goals), while efficiency is defined as ensuring most resources contribute to production without waste ('doing things right' or not wasting resources). Thus, a manager who is both reaches goals and does not waste resources.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 9 (Effectiveness means meeting goals) and Page 10 (Figure 1.6 matrix shows "Reaching goals and not wasting resources" in the Efficient/Effective quadrant).

questions.questionText: In any organization, change-related activities include

options.content: clarifying objectives of jobs in organizations
providing recognition for achievements and contributions

questions.explanation: According to the contemporary view of management skills, change-related activities are aimed at modifying organizational components. The textbook specifies that these include encouraging innovative thinking, monitoring the external environment, and proposing new strategies.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 12: "Change-related activities are management efforts aimed at modifying organizational components. Such activities include... encouraging innovative thinking..."

questions.questionText: This is an example of a(n)
questions.context: Trendy Garb is a retail store that sells women's apparel. The store has comprehensive rules, policies, and procedures for matters relating to customer complaints and product returns. Hence, when faced with either of these situations, the store manager simply needs to refer to these guidelines and proceed accordingly.
questions.explanation: Because the store has comprehensive, standard operating procedures, rules, and policies established for routine situations like returns and complaints, the manager is executing a programmed decision.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 182: "A programmed decision is routine and repetitive, and the organization typically develops specific ways to handle such decisions." Table 8.1 also lists 'Standard operating procedures' under programmed decisions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a traditional technique for solving a programmed decision?
questions.explanation: The traditional techniques for handling a programmed (routine) decision include 'Habit', 'Clerical routine' (standard operating procedures), and 'Organization structure'. Judgment, intuition, and rules of thumb are traditional techniques for nonprogrammed decisions.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 183: Table 8.1 lists 'Habit' under Traditional Decision-Making Techniques for Programmed decisions.

questions.questionText: ________ is the process of establishing orderly uses for resources within the management system.
questions.explanation: The formal definition of organizing is the process of establishing orderly uses for resources within the management system.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 249: "Organizing is the process of establishing orderly uses for all resources within the management system."

questions.questionText: ________ is the assignment of various portions of a particular task among a number of organization members.
questions.explanation: Division of labor is the specific term used to describe assigning portions of a single task among multiple workers.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 252: "Division of labor is the assignment of various portions of a particular task among a number of organization members."

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of division of labor?

options.content: It broadens the scope of work.
It results in high levels of employee motivation.
It emphasizes the human variable in organizations.

questions.explanation: A key advantage of division of labor is that workers stay in one place and do one job, meaning they do not lose valuable time changing tools or locations, which effectively saves time. The other options are actually problems associated with extreme division of labor.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 253: "Second, workers who concentrate on performing only one job naturally try to make the job easier and more efficient. Third, workers who are assigned to only one job do not lose valuable time in changing tools or locations."

questions.questionText: ________ is the initial attraction and screening of the supply of prospective human resources available to fill a position.
questions.explanation: The textbook explicitly defines recruitment exactly as the initial attraction and screening of the supply of prospective human resources available to fill a position.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 297: "Recruitment is the initial attraction and screening of the supply of prospective human resources available to fill a position."

questions.questionText: Which of the following items is likely to be found in a job specification?
questions.explanation: A Job Specification contains the human qualifications necessary to do the job, which explicitly includes 'Physical skills'. Job title, working conditions, equipment used, and job summary are all found in a Job Description.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 298 (Figure 13.2): Displays 'Job Specification' including 'Physical Skills'. The other options fall under 'Job Description'.

questions.questionText: ________ is the process of sharing information with other individuals.
questions.explanation: Communication is explicitly defined in the textbook as the process of sharing information with other individuals.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 348: "Communication is the process of sharing information with other individuals."

questions.questionText: The person in the interpersonal communication situation who originates and encodes information to be shared with another person is called the ________
questions.explanation: In the interpersonal communication process, the source (or source/encoder) is the individual who originates and encodes the information that is to be shared with another person.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 348: "The source/encoder is the person in the interpersonal communication situation who originates and encodes information to be shared with others."

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a communication macrobarrier?
questions.explanation: A macrobarrier is a factor hindering communication in a general situation. The "need for increasingly complex information" is specifically listed as a communication macrobarrier. The other options are considered microbarriers, which hinder communication in specific situations.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 350-351: "The following are among the macrobarriers... 2. The need for increasingly complex information."

questions.questionText: Which of the following is considered a microbarrier to organizational communication?
questions.explanation: Microbarriers hinder communication in specific situations. "Perception" (an individual's interpretation of a message) is explicitly listed as a microbarrier. The other options represent macrobarriers related to general societal and informational trends.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 351: "Among the microbarriers to successful communication are... 4. Perception."

questions.questionText: A formal group is a group that ________

options.content: is formed by management to perform organizational tasks
is formed by the common interests of group members
is formed by the affiliation of the group members

questions.explanation: A formal group is defined as a group "that exists within an organization by virtue of management decree to perform tasks that enhance the attainment of organizational objectives."
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 6.

questions.questionText: Formal groups that handle routine activities and are outlined on an organization chart are called ________
questions.explanation: A command group is a formal group that is outlined in the chain of command on an organization chart. They handle routine activities, unlike task groups which handle nonroutine tasks.
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 9.

questions.questionText: Two formal groups that are often established in organizations are ________ and ________
questions.explanation: While 'Command' and 'Task' are the primary categories of formal groups, 'Committees' are explicitly classified as a type of formal task group, and 'Work Teams' (as formal teams) are also established by organizations. Interest groups are informal.
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 10 (Committees) and Slide 18/19 (Teams).

questions.questionText: ________ is the systematic effort to compare performance to predetermined standards in order to determine whether performance is in line with those standards, or needs to be corrected.
questions.explanation: Roberto Mockler explicitly defines 'Controlling' as this exact systematic effort.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 502: "According to Roberto Mockler, controlling is a systematic effort by business management to compare performance to predetermined standards..."

questions.questionText: ________ and ________ have been called the "Siamese twins of management."
questions.explanation: The textbook explicitly states that planning and control are virtually inseparable functions and refers to them as the Siamese twins of management.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 502: "As implied by this definition, planning and control are virtually inseparable functions. In fact, these two functions have been called the Siamese twins of management."

questions.questionText: The level of activity established to serve as a model for evaluating organizational performance is a(n) ________
questions.explanation: A standard acts as the yardstick that determines whether organizational performance is adequate or inadequate. The textbook defines it exactly as the level of activity established to serve as a model for evaluation.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 505: "A standard is the level of activity established to serve as a model for evaluating organizational performance."

questions.questionText: ________ is managerial activity aimed at bringing organizational performance up to the level of performance standards.
questions.explanation: The textbook defines "Corrective action" exactly as managerial activity aimed at bringing organizational performance up to the level of performance standards.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 506: "Corrective action is managerial activity aimed at bringing organizational performance up to the level of performance standards."

questions.questionText: Because Jamie is the manager, her subordinates follow her instructions. This is an example of ________ power.
questions.explanation: Position power is the power derived strictly from the organizational position a manager holds. Since subordinates follow Jamie because she holds the official title and position of manager, it is an example of position power.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 508: "Position power is power derived from the organizational position a manager holds."

questions.questionText: The second step in the decision-making process is identifying a problem.
questions.explanation: In the rational decision-making process model, identifying an existing problem is the very first step, not the second. The second step is listing alternative problem solutions.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 186: "The decision-making steps this model depicts are as follows: 1. Identify an existing problem."

questions.questionText: In order to preserve their position power, managers should avoid doing personal favors for subordinates.
questions.explanation: Doing personal favors helps develop a sense of obligation, which increases a manager's "personal power." It does not negatively impact their "position power," which is determined by their formal rank in the organization.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 508: "To increase personal power, a manager should attempt to develop... A sense of obligation toward the manager... The basic strategy suggested for creating this sense of obligation is to do personal favors for people."

questions.questionText: Managers identify a problem by comparing the current state of affairs to some standard.
questions.explanation: The controlling process involves comparing measured performance to a standard. If the performance is significantly different from standards, the manager must take corrective action, which begins by recognizing the problem (a barrier to organizational goal attainment) that caused the deviation from the standard.
questions.reference: Textbook Pages 506-507 and the Controlling Process diagram on Page 504.

questions.questionText: intuitive decision making is systematic, logical, and orderly.
questions.explanation: Intuitive decision making (System 1) is fast, automatic, and based on an inborn ability to synthesize information quickly. It contrasts with rational decision making (System 2), which is systematic, logical, slow, comprehensive, and deliberate.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 190: "System 2 is a process described as being slow, comprehensive, and deliberate, while System 1 is described as being fast, automatic, and intuitive."

questions.questionText: A task group is a formal group outlined in the chain of command on an organization chart.
questions.explanation: This describes a 'Command Group'. A 'Task Group' is defined as a formal group of organization members who interact to accomplish nonroutine tasks.
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 9.

questions.questionText: Groupthink is a group decision-making process in which negative feedback on any suggested alternative by any group member is forbidden until all members have presented alternatives that they perceive as valuable.
questions.explanation: Groupthink is defined as "the mode of thinking that group members engage in when the desire for agreement so dominates the group that it overrides the need to realistically appraise alternative problem solutions." It is not a set of rules forbidding negative feedback.
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 16.

questions.questionText: Henri Fayol recommends that businesses establish multiple guiding authorities when organizing resources.
questions.explanation: Henri Fayol's principle of unity of command explicitly states that an individual should have only one boss. Establishing multiple guiding authorities contradicts this rule.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 260: "Fayol’s management principle of unity of command is the rationale for the existence of the scalar relationship. This principle recommends that an individual have only one boss."

questions.questionText: Bureaucracy can be characterized as a management system with detailed procedures, rules, and a clearly outlined organizational hierarchy with impersonal relationships among organization members.
questions.explanation: This perfectly matches Max Weber's bureaucratic model, which is defined by detailed procedures and rules, a clearly outlined hierarchy, and impersonal interactions designed to maximize efficiency.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 252: "Bureaucracy is the term Max Weber used to describe a management system that includes three primary components: detailed procedures and rules, a clearly outlined organizational hierarchy, and impersonal relationships among organization members."

questions.questionText: Vertical dimensioning is directly related to the concept of the scalar relationship that is, the chain of command.
questions.explanation: Vertical dimensioning deals with the levels of authority within an organization. This is directly built on the scalar relationship (chain of command), which traces authority from the highest level down to the lowest.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 260: "Vertical dimensioning refers to the extent to which an organization uses vertical levels to separate job responsibilities. Vertical dimensioning is directly related to the concept of the scalar relationship—that is, the chain of command."

questions.questionText: The matrix structure is contradictory to the principle of unity of command.
questions.explanation: In a matrix structure, employees report to both a project manager and a functional manager. This explicitly contradicts the unity of command principle, which states an employee should have only one boss.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 267: "An organization that adopts a matrix structure contradicts the principle of unity of command (which states that an individual should have only one boss)..."

questions.questionText: The basic elements of the interpersonal communication process are the source, the encoder, and the decoder.
questions.explanation: The statement is false because it omits the "signal." The three basic elements of the interpersonal communication process are the source/encoder, the signal, and the decoder/destination.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 348: "To be a successful interpersonal communicator, a manager must understand the three basic elements of interpersonal communication: the source/encoder, the signal, and the decoder/destination."

questions.questionText: The ideal number of committee members for most tasks seems to be from 15 to 20.
questions.explanation: While the slides mention that the "optimum size of the committee should be determined," standard management theory (and typically associated text for this course) suggests much smaller numbers (usually 5-7 members) to maintain efficiency and prevent social loafing. 15 to 20 members is generally considered too large for effective decision-making.
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Inferred from Slide 14 and general management principles regarding committee size.

questions.questionText: An interest group is an informal group that forms in organizations because of the personal affiliation members have with one another.
questions.explanation: An informal group that forms because of personal affiliation is defined as a "Friendship Group." An "Interest Group" gains membership primarily because of a common concern members have about a specific issue.
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 21.

questions.questionText: Communication is considered a supplementary management skill rather than a fundamental management skill.
questions.explanation: The textbook indicates that chief executives rank communication skills extremely high—tying for first place as the most important skill to teach management students. Thus, it is a fundamental, not supplementary, management skill.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 351: "Table 15.1 shows that chief executives rank communication skills... tying for rank 1 as the most important skill that should be taught to management students."

questions.questionText: Good communicators consult with others when planning communications.
questions.explanation: According to the guidelines for achieving communication effectiveness (the "Ten Commandments of Good Communication"), managers should consult with others, when appropriate, while planning their communications to gain additional insights and ensure clarity.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 353: "4. Consult with others, where appropriate, in planning communications."

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is true about corporate social responsibility?

options.content: It is the managerial obligation to ensure the accountability of certain individuals in an organization through mechanisms that try to reduce or eliminate the principal-agent problem.
It is the managerial obligation to cater to the needs of the stockholders, while abiding by the laws of the society.
It is the managerial obligation to take action that protects and improves both the welfare of society as a whole and the interests of the organization.
It is the managerial obligation to abide to societal laws when pursuing organizational goals.
It is the managerial obligation to ensure ethical decision-making in an organization to benefit its customers.

questions.explanation: The textbook explicitly defines corporate social responsibility exactly as the managerial obligation to take action that protects and improves both the welfare of society as a whole and the interests of the organization. The slides highlight that acting ethically toward all stakeholders improves corporate health.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 52: "corporate social responsibility is the managerial obligation to take action that protects and improves both the welfare of society as a whole and the interests of the organization." Slides 7 and 9 reflect this through stakeholder relations.

questions.questionText: ____ and ____ have been called the "Siamese twins of management."
questions.explanation: Planning and controlling are deeply interdependent. Planning sets the standards, and controlling measures performance against them. They are famously referred to as the Siamese twins of management.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 161 (and referenced in Control chapters): "Planning and controlling are virtually inseparable functions... they have been called the Siamese twins of management."

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about decisions and decision-making?

options.content: Managers make decisions primarily when performing the controlling function.
In the process of deciding, the alternatives are as important as the choice made.
Organizations only have to consider significant decisions that have a major impact on business.
Decision making is the process of choosing the best alternative for reaching objectives.
All managerial decisions are of equal significance to the organization.

questions.explanation: The textbook specifically provides the definition of decision making verbatim as the process of choosing the best alternative for reaching objectives. Other options are false: decisions are made across all functions, not just controlling, and managerial decisions vary greatly in significance.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 182: "Decision making is the process of choosing the best alternative for reaching objectives."

questions.questionText: The level of activity established to serve as a model for evaluating organizational performance is a(n)
questions.explanation: This is the exact, verbatim definition of a "standard" provided in the textbook.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 505: "A standard is the level of activity established to serve as a model for evaluating organizational performance."

questions.questionText: This is an example of a(n)
questions.context: Trendy Garb is a retail store that sells women's apparel. The store has comprehensive rules, policies, and procedures for matters relating to customer complaints and product returns. Hence, when faced with either of these situations, the store manager simply needs to refer to these guidelines and proceed accordingly.
questions.explanation: This scenario demonstrates a routine and repetitive problem handled by standard operating procedures (rules and policies), which perfectly aligns with the textbook definition of a programmed decision.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 182: "A programmed decision is routine and repetitive, and the organization typically develops specific ways to handle such decisions."

questions.questionText: Nonprogrammed decisions are
questions.explanation: Nonprogrammed decisions are defined in the text as one-shot, ill-structured, or novel policy decisions used to handle unique situations.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 182: "In contrast, a nonprogrammed decision is typically a one-shot decision that is usually less structured than programmed decisions."

questions.questionText: Which of the following is least accurate regarding groups?

options.content: They are found in all organizations.
An understanding of groups can help managers raise the probability that the groups will cause desirable consequences for the organization.
Groups inevitably form in all facets of organizational existence.
Groups invariably cause desirable consequences within the organization.
Groups are characterized by a size small enough to permit each member to communicate with all other members on a face-to-face basis.

questions.explanation: The slides explicitly state that "Groups can cause either desirable or undesirable consequences within the organization." Therefore, stating that they "invariably" (always) cause desirable consequences is inaccurate.
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 5.

questions.questionText: ____ is the management function through which managers compare present performance to preestablished performance standards.
questions.explanation: Controlling is the management function that utilizes a systematic effort to compare performance to predetermined standards to verify if performance is in line.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 502: "According to Roberto Mockler, controlling is a systematic effort by business management to compare performance to predetermined standards..."

questions.questionText: Which of the following arguments provided by Milton Friedman suggests that corporate social responsibility may be unethical?

options.content: Corporate social responsibility compels managers to spend money on some individuals that rightfully belongs to other individuals.
Corporate social responsibility is not mandated by law, which means that it has to be done by will, not by compulsion.
Empirical studies have not yet demonstrated a definitive relationship between corporate social responsibility and profitability.
Profitability and growth go hand-in-hand with responsible treatment of employees, customers, and the community.
Firms use corporate social responsibility to increase their brand awareness.

questions.explanation: Milton Friedman argues that making managers pursue socially responsible objectives may be unethical because it forces them to spend money (which rightfully belongs to the owners/shareholders) on other individuals or general societal causes, setting up a direct conflict of interest.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 55: "Friedman also argues that to require business managers to pursue socially responsible objectives may, in fact, be unethical, because it compels managers to spend money on some individuals that rightfully belongs to other individuals." Slide 9 aligns with this by emphasizing the opportunity to make a "fair profit".

questions.questionText: ____ includes determining tasks and groupings of work. It should not be rigid, but adaptable and flexible to meet challenges as circumstances change.
questions.explanation: Organizing inherently involves establishing tasks and forming departments (groupings of work). Henri Fayol advised that strict adherence to formal structures is not always advisable, highlighting that organizing should remain adaptable and flexible.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 261: "Fayol’s Advice on Using Formal Structure: Henri Fayol has indicated that strict adherence to a particular chain of command is not always advisable... organizations should be adaptable and flexible."

questions.questionText: Managers can fulfill their social obligation towards consumers by

options.content: increasing the value of the organization

questions.explanation: According to the textbook's breakdown of stakeholders and corresponding social obligations, the specific obligation a manager owes to consumers is to provide safe products. Abiding by laws is owed to government agencies, providing safe working environments is owed to employees, and repaying debts is owed to lenders.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 58 (Table 3.2): Stakeholder: Consumers -> Social Obligations Owed: To provide safe products. Slide 9 echoes this via the Johnson & Johnson Credo.

questions.questionText: As part of the controlling process, you have finished measuring the performance of your team. What must you do next?

options.content: Establish a unit of measure to gauge performance.

questions.explanation: Step 1 of the controlling process is measuring performance. Step 2 is explicitly comparing that measured performance to established standards.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 503: "As Figure 21.2 illustrates, there are three main steps in the controlling process: 1. Measuring performance 2. Comparing measured performance to standards..."

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a communication macrobarrier?
questions.explanation: A macrobarrier is a factor hindering communication in a general situation. The "need for increasingly complex information" is specifically listed as a communication macrobarrier. The other options are considered microbarriers, which hinder communication in specific situations.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 350-351: "The following are among the macrobarriers... 2. The need for increasingly complex information."

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is true for the management function?

options.content: It reaches goals by working with and through people.
It is a one-time function in an organization.
It is a series of continuing and unrelated activities.
It involves-and concentrates on reaching individual goals.
It does not consider the people aspect of organizations.

questions.explanation: The official definition of management states that it is the continuous process of reaching organizational goals by working with and through people and utilizing other organizational resources.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 6: "...management is the process of reaching organizational goals by working with and through people and other organizational resources."

questions.questionText: Formal groups are commonly divided into ____ and ____
questions.explanation: The two kinds of Formal Groups listed are the Command Group and the Task Group.
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 9.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is true about organizing?

options.content: It is the process of determining how the organization will achieve its objectives.
It is the management process of guiding the activities of organization members to help attain organizational objectives.
It is the process of making things happen as they were planned to happen.
It is the process of establishing orderly uses for all the organization's resources.

questions.explanation: The textbook directly defines organizing as the process of establishing orderly uses for resources within the management system.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 249: "Organizing is the process of establishing orderly uses for all resources within the management system."

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a traditional technique for solving a programmed decision?
questions.explanation: The traditional techniques for solving programmed decisions include Habit, Clerical routine, and Organization structure. Judgment, intuition, and rules of thumb belong to nonprogrammed decisions.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 183: Table 8.1 lists 'Habit' under Traditional Decision-Making Techniques for Programmed decisions.

questions.questionText: Encoded information the source intends to share with another person is called a(n)
questions.explanation: According to the textbook's definition, the encoded information itself that the source intends to share with someone else constitutes a message. When it is transmitted, it becomes a signal.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 348: "Encoded information that the source intends to share constitutes a message."

questions.questionText: In which of the following stages of performing social responsibility activities does a manager lead, communicate, motivate, and work with groups to attain the organization's social responsibility objectives?
questions.explanation: Influencing is the management function that focuses on guiding the activities of organization members, which involves leading, communicating, motivating, and working with groups to achieve organizational objectives.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 346: "Influencing is the process of guiding the activities of organization members in appropriate directions... The ability to communicate, lead, motivate, and manage groups is critical to the influencing subsystem."

questions.questionText: In business, ethics can be defined as

options.content: the capacity to reflect on customer preferences in the corporate decision-making process
the capacity to reflect on competitive strategies-in the corporate decision-making process
the capacity to reflect on values in the corporate decision-making process
the capacity to reflect on production bottlenecks in the corporate decision-making process
the capacity to reflect on workforce diversity in the corporate decision-making process

questions.explanation: Both the textbook and the lecture slides explicitly define business ethics as the capacity to reflect on values in the corporate decision-making process, to determine how these values and decisions affect various stakeholder groups.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 63: "In business, ethics can be defined as the capacity to reflect on values in the corporate decision-making process..." Slide 5 provides the exact same definition.

questions.questionText: ____ is a formal statement that acts as a guide for the ethics of how people within a particular organization should act and make decisions.
questions.explanation: A code of ethics is precisely defined in both the textbook and lecture materials as a formal statement that acts as a guide for the ethics of how people within a particular organization should act and make decisions.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 64: "A code of ethics is a formal statement that acts as a guide for the ethics of how people within a particular organization should act and make decisions." Slide 11 provides the exact same definition.

questions.questionText: Which of the following actions suggests that an individual is following the golden rule?

options.content: Acting in a way you would expect others to act toward you.
Taking actions that would be viewed as proper by a disinterested panel of professional peers.
Acting in a way that results in the greatest good for the greatest number of people.
Taking actions that abide by the laws of the state.
Acting in a way that the action taken under the circumstances could be a universal law of behavior.

questions.explanation: The Golden Rule is a fundamental ethical standard defined as acting in a way you would expect others to act toward you. The other options refer to the professional ethic, the utilitarian principle, the legal test, and Kant's categorical imperative, respectively.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 66: "1. The golden rule: Act in a way you would expect others to act toward you." Slide 15 provides the exact same definition.

questions.questionText: Name one of the basic concepts for smoothly running an organisation.

options.content: None of the options is correct

questions.explanation: Management is the overarching concept and process whose primary role is to smoothly guide the organization towards its goals by effectively utilizing its resources through the execution of its core functions.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 5: "Essentially, the role of managers is to guide organizations toward goal accomplishment... Management moves an organization toward its purposes or goals by assigning activities organization members perform."

questions.questionText: An informal group that gains and maintains membership primarily because of a common concern members have about a specific issue is called
questions.explanation: This is the exact definition provided for an "Interest Group".
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 21.

questions.questionText: At what step of the planning can be processed with the topmost and applicable plan would be implemented?
questions.explanation: Despite the flawed wording in option 'c' ('Selecting up objective' instead of 'Selecting an alternative'), Step 4 of the planning process involves choosing the best alternative (the topmost/applicable plan) for implementation.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 164 (The Planning Process): "Step 4: Choose best alternative for reaching objectives."

questions.questionText: A work team composed of people from different functional areas of the organization who are all focused on a specified objective is known as a
questions.explanation: While 'cross-functional team' is not explicitly defined in the provided slides, it is the standard management term for a team composed of members from different functional areas. A 'task group' is broader, simply defining a group formed for a nonroutine task.
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Standard management terminology (Inferred from the context of Teams vs Groups on Slide 19).

questions.questionText: In which pace of the planning process, two sides of a coin of each alternative are examined.
questions.explanation: Evaluating alternatives involves analyzing the pros and cons (the two sides of the coin) of each listed option before making a final selection.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 164: Evaluating alternatives is the step where managers assess the benefits and drawbacks of each potential course of action.

questions.questionText: One of the benefits of utilizing committees is that

options.content: the decision-making process is much quicker than individual decision-making
there is no limit on the size of the committee
a committee does need a leader or a secretary
committees improve the quality of decision-making
decision-makers don't have to represent the group they come from

questions.explanation: The slides list "Committees can improve the quality of decision making" as one of the primary reasons managers should use committees.
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 12.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is considered the first step toward effective communication?

options.content: clarifying the idea or problem to be communicated
examining the true purpose of communication
consulting with others in planning communication
identifying actions that support the message being communicated
understanding the total physical and human setting

questions.explanation: The first of the "Ten Commandments of Good Communication" states that communicators should systematically analyze and clarify their ideas or problems before communicating. This clarification is the first step toward effective communication.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 353: "1. Seek to clarify your ideas before communicating... This is the first step toward effective communication."

questions.questionText: It is known as planning.

options.content: The last function of the manager
None of the options is correct

questions.explanation: Because of the concept of the 'Primacy of Planning', planning is considered the primary, or first, function a manager must perform.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 161: "Planning is the primary management function—the one that precedes and is the basis for the organizing, influencing, and controlling functions."

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a purely procedural step that could be taken to increase the probability that a committee will be successful?

options.content: specifying the authority of the committee
bringing all members into active participation
keeping the goals of the group flexible

questions.explanation: Under 'Procedural Steps' for committee success, "The committee's authority should be specified" is explicitly listed. Rephrasing, bringing members into participation, and stimulating thought are 'People-Oriented Guidelines'.
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 14.

questions.questionText: Thinking for the future output is known as

options.content: All of the options are correct

questions.explanation: Developing or setting planning premises involves making assumptions about the future conditions upon which alternative plans will be based. It is essentially thinking about future scenarios.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 164: Step 3 of the Planning Process involves "Develop premises upon which each alternative is based... a premise is an assumption upon which the alternative is based."

questions.questionText: What is the major purpose of feedback in the communication process?

options.content: It is used by the source to ensure successful communication.
It can be used to boost the legitimate power of managers.
It provides formal documentation of the communication process.
It helps the source avoid questions from the destination.
It fosters lateral communication in the organization.

questions.explanation: Feedback is the destination's reaction to a message. The major purpose of gathering this feedback is so the source can determine whether the destination derived the intended meaning, thus ensuring successful communication.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 350: "Feedback is the destination's reaction to a message. It can be used by the source to ensure successful communication."

questions.questionText: The person in the interpersonal communication situation who originates and encodes information to be shared with another person is called the
questions.explanation: In the interpersonal communication process, the source (or source/encoder) is the individual who originates and encodes the information that is to be shared with another person.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 348: "The source/encoder is the person in the interpersonal communication situation who originates and encodes information to be shared with others."

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an interest group?

options.content: a group of friends interested in interested in rock music
a group meeting to consider the feasibility of a new product
a group meeting to prepare the monthly financial reports
a group of workers pressing management for better pay

questions.explanation: An interest group forms because members share a common concern about a specific issue (e.g., pressing management for better pay). A group of friends listening to music is a Friendship Group. The other options are formal Task or Command groups.
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Based on the definition of Interest Group on Slide 21.

questions.questionText: What is the core of making a plan?
questions.explanation: Planning is inherently future-oriented. It involves determining how the organization can get where it wants to go, which requires analyzing foreseen opportunities and thinking in advance.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 159: "Planning is the process of determining how the organization can get where it wants to go..." which fundamentally requires thinking in advance.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements about groupthink is true?

options.content: Groupthink cannot take place in a newly formed group.
A group with high levels of mistrust and conflicts is likely to be most susceptible to groupthink.
A group with a high level of cohesiveness is likely to be susceptible to groupthink.
Managers must help committees to establish groupthink to generate alternative problem solutions.
A group which is highly competitive will most probably result in groupthink.

questions.explanation: Groupthink occurs when the "desire for agreement so dominates the group that it overrides the need to realistically appraise alternative problem solutions." High cohesiveness creates this strong desire for agreement and conformity, making the group highly susceptible to groupthink.
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Inferred from the definition and symptoms of Groupthink on Slide 16.

questions.questionText: At what stage of the planning becomes the most feasible plan that can be implemented.
questions.explanation: After evaluating options, the manager chooses the best (most feasible) alternative to reach the objectives, which is then developed into actionable plans.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 164: Step 4 of the Planning Process is "Choose best alternative for reaching objectives."

questions.questionText: ____ is the process of sharing information with other individuals.
questions.explanation: Communication is explicitly defined in the textbook as the process of sharing information with other individuals.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 348: "Communication is the process of sharing information with other individuals."

questions.questionText: Planning establishes a ground standard for
questions.explanation: Planning establishes the objectives and standards that the Controlling function then uses to measure actual performance against to determine if goals are being met.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 161 (and referenced in Control chapters): Planning is the basis for controlling, as controlling compares performance against the standards set during planning.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of division of labor?

options.content: It results in easier and more efficient work.
It broadens the scope of work.
It emphasizes the human variable in organizations.
It results in high levels of employee motivation.

questions.explanation: An explicit advantage of division of labor is that when workers concentrate on performing only one job, they naturally try to make the job easier and more efficient.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 253: "Second, workers who concentrate on performing only one job naturally try to make the job easier and more efficient."

questions.questionText: Define the term premises?
questions.explanation: In the context of the planning process, developing premises means formulating assumptions about future conditions and environments upon which alternative plans will be based.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 164: "a premise is an assumption upon which the alternative is based."

questions.questionText: Which of the following is one of the three main components of the management system that Weber termed a bureaucracy?

options.content: close, personal relations among organization members

questions.explanation: Weber's bureaucratic model includes three main concepts: detailed procedures and rules, impersonal relationships, and a clearly outlined organizational hierarchy.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 252: "Bureaucracy is the term Max Weber used to describe a management system that includes three primary components: detailed procedures and rules, a clearly outlined organizational hierarchy, and impersonal relationships among organization members."

questions.questionText: An individual's emotional intelligence is characterized by self-awareness, self-motivation, self-regulation, empathy for others, and
questions.explanation: According to Daniel Goleman's concept of emotional intelligence, it is characterized by five key traits: self-awareness, self-motivation, self-regulation, empathy for others, and adeptness in building relationships.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 347: "Goleman characterizes an individual's emotional intelligence as being characterized by self-awareness, self-motivation, self-regulation, empathy for others, and adeptness in building relationships."

questions.questionText: ____ is the mode of thinking that group members engage in when the desire for agreement so dominates the group that it overrides the need to realistically appraise alternative problem solutions.
questions.explanation: This is the exact definition of Groupthink provided in the lecture.
questions.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found verbatim on Slide 16.

questions.questionText: ____ resources refer to the machines used during the manufacturing process.
questions.explanation: In the breakdown of organizational resources, the textbook explicitly defines 'Capital resources' as the machines or equipment used directly in the manufacturing process to maintain desired production levels.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 8: "Capital resources are machines used during the manufacturing process. Modern machines, or equipment, can be a major factor in maintaining desired production levels."

questions.questionText: This role performed by Trot can be called
questions.context: Trot is the CEO of a consulting firm. He plays a key role in guiding the activities of organization members in appropriate directions.
questions.explanation: The textbook formally defines influencing as the process of guiding the activities of organization members in appropriate directions. Trot's role perfectly aligns with this definition.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 346: "Influencing is the process of guiding the activities of organization members in appropriate directions."

questions.questionText: Organizational communication that does not follow the lines of the organizational chart is specifically called
questions.explanation: Informal organizational communication is specifically defined as communication that does not follow the formal lines of the organization chart, but rather follows the pattern of personal relationships.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 355: "Informal organizational communication does not follow the lines of the organization chart."

questions.questionText: ____ skills are very important to managers at the lower, middle and top levels.
questions.explanation: According to the classic view of management skills, while the need for technical and conceptual skills varies depending on the management level, 'Human Skills' remain highly and equally important across top, middle, and supervisory levels.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 11: "Human skills, however, are extremely important to managers at top, middle, and lower (or supervisory) levels. The common denominator of all management levels, after all, is people."

questions.questionText: This is a fault in the ____ function of management.
questions.context: Gayle has not established appropriate performance standards for her team.
questions.explanation: Establishing and utilizing performance standards is a core component of the "Comparing Measured Performance To Standards" step within the controlling process. Failing to establish appropriate standards prevents successful controlling.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 505: "Comparing Measured Performance to Standards... A standard is the level of activity established to serve as a model for evaluating organizational performance."

questions.questionText: The more resources unused during the production process, the more ____ the manager.
questions.explanation: Managerial efficiency deals directly with the proportion of resources contributing to productivity. The textbook explicitly correlates wasted or unused resources with managerial inefficiency.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 10: "The more resources wasted or unused during the production process, the more inefficient is the manager."

questions.questionText: Controlling does not highlight the deviations in the process.
questions.explanation: The entire purpose of control and comparing measured performance to standards is to signal or highlight when deviations from the plan are occurring so that corrective action can be taken.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 502: "We must develop methods of measurement and control to signal when deviations from the plan are occurring so that corrective action can be taken."

questions.questionText: Organizing is the process of establishing orderly uses for all resources within the management system.
questions.explanation: This is the exact, verbatim definition of organizing provided in the textbook.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 249: "Organizing is the process of establishing orderly uses for all resources within the management system."

questions.questionText: Vertical dimensioning is directly related to the concept of the scalar relationship that is, the chain of command.
questions.explanation: Vertical dimensioning encompasses the scalar relationship (chain of command), mapping how authority scales downward from the individual at the top to those at the bottom.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 260: "Vertical dimensioning refers to the extent to which an organization uses vertical levels to separate job responsibilities. Vertical dimensioning is directly related to the concept of the scalar relationship—that is, the chain of command."

questions.questionText: Corrective actions are necessary after analyzing the deviations.
questions.explanation: If the comparison step shows that performance is significantly different from standards (a deviation), the required next step in the controlling process is to take corrective action to bring performance up to the standard.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 506: "After actual performance has been measured and compared with established performance standards, the next step in the controlling process is to take corrective action if necessary."

questions.questionText: Human skills, unlike technical skills, involve the ability to see the organization as a whole.
questions.explanation: The ability to see the organization as a whole is defined as 'Conceptual Skills', whereas 'Human Skills' deal with the ability to work effectively with people.
questions.reference: Textbook Page 11: "Conceptual skills involve the ability to see the organization as a whole."

questions.questionText: An organization that wants to retain an employee may need to assist that employee's spouse in his or her career development as well.
