2024:Q18.explanation: The textbook specifically provides the definition of decision making verbatim as the process of choosing the best alternative for reaching objectives. Other options are false: decisions are made across all functions, not just controlling, and managerial decisions vary greatly in significance.
2024:Q18.reference: Textbook Page 182: "Decision making is the process of choosing the best alternative for reaching objectives."

2024:Q19.questionText: The level of activity established to serve as a model for evaluating organizational performance is a(n)
2024:Q19.explanation: This is the exact, verbatim definition of a "standard" provided in the textbook.
2024:Q19.reference: Textbook Page 505: "A standard is the level of activity established to serve as a model for evaluating organizational performance."

2024:Q20.questionText: This is an example of a(n)
2024:Q20.context: Trendy Garb is a retail store that sells women's apparel. The store has comprehensive rules, policies, and procedures for matters relating to customer complaints and product returns. Hence, when faced with either of these situations, the store manager simply needs to refer to these guidelines and proceed accordingly.
2024:Q20.explanation: This scenario demonstrates a routine and repetitive problem handled by standard operating procedures (rules and policies), which perfectly aligns with the textbook definition of a programmed decision.
2024:Q20.reference: Textbook Page 182: "A programmed decision is routine and repetitive, and the organization typically develops specific ways to handle such decisions."

2024:Q21.explanation: Nonprogrammed decisions are defined in the text as one-shot, ill-structured, or novel policy decisions used to handle unique situations.
2024:Q21.reference: Textbook Page 182: "In contrast, a nonprogrammed decision is typically a one-shot decision that is usually less structured than programmed decisions."

2024:Q22.questionText: Which of the following is least accurate regarding groups?

options.content: They are found in all organizations.
An understanding of groups can help managers raise the probability that the groups will cause desirable consequences for the organization.
Groups inevitably form in all facets of organizational existence.
Groups invariably cause desirable consequences within the organization.
Groups are characterized by a size small enough to permit each member to communicate with all other members on a face-to-face basis.

2024:Q22.explanation: The slides explicitly state that "Groups can cause either desirable or undesirable consequences within the organization." Therefore, stating that they "invariably" (always) cause desirable consequences is inaccurate.
2024:Q22.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 5.

2024:Q23.questionText: ____ is the management function through which managers compare present performance to preestablished performance standards.
2024:Q23.explanation: Controlling is the management function that utilizes a systematic effort to compare performance to predetermined standards to verify if performance is in line.
2024:Q23.reference: Textbook Page 502: "According to Roberto Mockler, controlling is a systematic effort by business management to compare performance to predetermined standards..."

2024:Q24.questionText: Which of the following arguments provided by Milton Friedman suggests that corporate social responsibility may be unethical?

options.content: Corporate social responsibility compels managers to spend money on some individuals that rightfully belongs to other individuals.
Corporate social responsibility is not mandated by law, which means that it has to be done by will, not by compulsion.
Empirical studies have not yet demonstrated a definitive relationship between corporate social responsibility and profitability.
Profitability and growth go hand-in-hand with responsible treatment of employees, customers, and the community.
Firms use corporate social responsibility to increase their brand awareness.

2024:Q24.explanation: Milton Friedman argues that making managers pursue socially responsible objectives may be unethical because it forces them to spend money (which rightfully belongs to the owners/shareholders) on other individuals or general societal causes, setting up a direct conflict of interest.
2024:Q24.reference: Textbook Page 55: "Friedman also argues that to require business managers to pursue socially responsible objectives may, in fact, be unethical, because it compels managers to spend money on some individuals that rightfully belongs to other individuals." Slide 9 aligns with this by emphasizing the opportunity to make a "fair profit".

2024:Q25.questionText: ____ includes determining tasks and groupings of work. It should not be rigid, but adaptable and flexible to meet challenges as circumstances change.
2024:Q25.explanation: Organizing inherently involves establishing tasks and forming departments (groupings of work). Henri Fayol advised that strict adherence to formal structures is not always advisable, highlighting that organizing should remain adaptable and flexible.
2024:Q25.reference: Textbook Page 261: "Fayol’s Advice on Using Formal Structure: Henri Fayol has indicated that strict adherence to a particular chain of command is not always advisable... organizations should be adaptable and flexible."

2024:Q26.questionText: Managers can fulfill their social obligation towards consumers by

options.content: increasing the value of the organization

2024:Q26.explanation: According to the textbook's breakdown of stakeholders and corresponding social obligations, the specific obligation a manager owes to consumers is to provide safe products. Abiding by laws is owed to government agencies, providing safe working environments is owed to employees, and repaying debts is owed to lenders.
2024:Q26.reference: Textbook Page 58 (Table 3.2): Stakeholder: Consumers -> Social Obligations Owed: To provide safe products. Slide 9 echoes this via the Johnson & Johnson Credo.

2024:Q27.questionText: As part of the controlling process, you have finished measuring the performance of your team. What must you do next?

options.content: Establish a unit of measure to gauge performance.

2024:Q27.explanation: Step 1 of the controlling process is measuring performance. Step 2 is explicitly comparing that measured performance to established standards.
2024:Q27.reference: Textbook Page 503: "As Figure 21.2 illustrates, there are three main steps in the controlling process: 1. Measuring performance 2. Comparing measured performance to standards..."

2024:Q28.questionText: Which of the following is a communication macrobarrier?
2024:Q28.explanation: A macrobarrier is a factor hindering communication in a general situation. The "need for increasingly complex information" is specifically listed as a communication macrobarrier. The other options are considered microbarriers, which hinder communication in specific situations.
2024:Q28.reference: Textbook Page 350-351: "The following are among the macrobarriers... 2. The need for increasingly complex information."

2024:Q29.questionText: Which of the following statements is true for the management function?

options.content: It reaches goals by working with and through people.
It is a one-time function in an organization.
It is a series of continuing and unrelated activities.
It involves-and concentrates on reaching individual goals.
It does not consider the people aspect of organizations.

2024:Q29.explanation: The official definition of management states that it is the continuous process of reaching organizational goals by working with and through people and utilizing other organizational resources.
2024:Q29.reference: Textbook Page 6: "...management is the process of reaching organizational goals by working with and through people and other organizational resources."

2024:Q30.questionText: Formal groups are commonly divided into ____ and ____
2024:Q30.explanation: The two kinds of Formal Groups listed are the Command Group and the Task Group.
2024:Q30.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 9.

2024:Q31.questionText: Which of the following statements is true about organizing?

options.content: It is the process of determining how the organization will achieve its objectives.
It is the management process of guiding the activities of organization members to help attain organizational objectives.
It is the process of making things happen as they were planned to happen.
It is the process of establishing orderly uses for all the organization's resources.

2024:Q31.explanation: The textbook directly defines organizing as the process of establishing orderly uses for resources within the management system.
2024:Q31.reference: Textbook Page 249: "Organizing is the process of establishing orderly uses for all resources within the management system."

2024:Q32.questionText: Which of the following is a traditional technique for solving a programmed decision?
2024:Q32.explanation: The traditional techniques for solving programmed decisions include Habit, Clerical routine, and Organization structure. Judgment, intuition, and rules of thumb belong to nonprogrammed decisions.
2024:Q32.reference: Textbook Page 183: Table 8.1 lists 'Habit' under Traditional Decision-Making Techniques for Programmed decisions.

2024:Q33.questionText: Encoded information the source intends to share with another person is called a(n)
2024:Q33.explanation: According to the textbook's definition, the encoded information itself that the source intends to share with someone else constitutes a message. When it is transmitted, it becomes a signal.
2024:Q33.reference: Textbook Page 348: "Encoded information that the source intends to share constitutes a message."

2024:Q34.questionText: In which of the following stages of performing social responsibility activities does a manager lead, communicate, motivate, and work with groups to attain the organization's social responsibility objectives?
2024:Q34.explanation: Influencing is the management function that focuses on guiding the activities of organization members, which involves leading, communicating, motivating, and working with groups to achieve organizational objectives.
2024:Q34.reference: Textbook Page 346: "Influencing is the process of guiding the activities of organization members in appropriate directions... The ability to communicate, lead, motivate, and manage groups is critical to the influencing subsystem."

2024:Q35.questionText: In business, ethics can be defined as

options.content: the capacity to reflect on customer preferences in the corporate decision-making process
the capacity to reflect on competitive strategies-in the corporate decision-making process
the capacity to reflect on values in the corporate decision-making process
the capacity to reflect on production bottlenecks in the corporate decision-making process
the capacity to reflect on workforce diversity in the corporate decision-making process

2024:Q35.explanation: Both the textbook and the lecture slides explicitly define business ethics as the capacity to reflect on values in the corporate decision-making process, to determine how these values and decisions affect various stakeholder groups.
2024:Q35.reference: Textbook Page 63: "In business, ethics can be defined as the capacity to reflect on values in the corporate decision-making process..." Slide 5 provides the exact same definition.

2024:Q36.questionText: ____ is a formal statement that acts as a guide for the ethics of how people within a particular organization should act and make decisions.
2024:Q36.explanation: A code of ethics is precisely defined in both the textbook and lecture materials as a formal statement that acts as a guide for the ethics of how people within a particular organization should act and make decisions.
2024:Q36.reference: Textbook Page 64: "A code of ethics is a formal statement that acts as a guide for the ethics of how people within a particular organization should act and make decisions." Slide 11 provides the exact same definition.

2024:Q37.questionText: Which of the following actions suggests that an individual is following the golden rule?

options.content: Acting in a way you would expect others to act toward you.
Taking actions that would be viewed as proper by a disinterested panel of professional peers.
Acting in a way that results in the greatest good for the greatest number of people.
Taking actions that abide by the laws of the state.
Acting in a way that the action taken under the circumstances could be a universal law of behavior.

2024:Q37.explanation: The Golden Rule is a fundamental ethical standard defined as acting in a way you would expect others to act toward you. The other options refer to the professional ethic, the utilitarian principle, the legal test, and Kant's categorical imperative, respectively.
2024:Q37.reference: Textbook Page 66: "1. The golden rule: Act in a way you would expect others to act toward you." Slide 15 provides the exact same definition.

2024:Q38.questionText: Name one of the basic concepts for smoothly running an organisation.

options.content: None of the options is correct

2024:Q38.explanation: Management is the overarching concept and process whose primary role is to smoothly guide the organization towards its goals by effectively utilizing its resources through the execution of its core functions.
2024:Q38.reference: Textbook Page 5: "Essentially, the role of managers is to guide organizations toward goal accomplishment... Management moves an organization toward its purposes or goals by assigning activities organization members perform."

2024:Q39.questionText: An informal group that gains and maintains membership primarily because of a common concern members have about a specific issue is called
2024:Q39.explanation: This is the exact definition provided for an "Interest Group".
2024:Q39.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 21.

2024:Q40.questionText: At what step of the planning can be processed with the topmost and applicable plan would be implemented?
2024:Q40.explanation: Despite the flawed wording in option 'c' ('Selecting up objective' instead of 'Selecting an alternative'), Step 4 of the planning process involves choosing the best alternative (the topmost/applicable plan) for implementation.
2024:Q40.reference: Textbook Page 164 (The Planning Process): "Step 4: Choose best alternative for reaching objectives."

2024:Q41.questionText: A work team composed of people from different functional areas of the organization who are all focused on a specified objective is known as a
2024:Q41.explanation: While 'cross-functional team' is not explicitly defined in the provided slides, it is the standard management term for a team composed of members from different functional areas. A 'task group' is broader, simply defining a group formed for a nonroutine task.
2024:Q41.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Standard management terminology (Inferred from the context of Teams vs Groups on Slide 19).

2024:Q42.questionText: In which pace of the planning process, two sides of a coin of each alternative are examined.
2024:Q42.explanation: Evaluating alternatives involves analyzing the pros and cons (the two sides of the coin) of each listed option before making a final selection.
2024:Q42.reference: Textbook Page 164: Evaluating alternatives is the step where managers assess the benefits and drawbacks of each potential course of action.

2024:Q43.questionText: One of the benefits of utilizing committees is that

options.content: the decision-making process is much quicker than individual decision-making
there is no limit on the size of the committee
a committee does need a leader or a secretary
committees improve the quality of decision-making
decision-makers don't have to represent the group they come from

2024:Q43.explanation: The slides list "Committees can improve the quality of decision making" as one of the primary reasons managers should use committees.
2024:Q43.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 12.

2024:Q44.questionText: Which of the following is considered the first step toward effective communication?

options.content: clarifying the idea or problem to be communicated
examining the true purpose of communication
consulting with others in planning communication
identifying actions that support the message being communicated
understanding the total physical and human setting

2024:Q44.explanation: The first of the "Ten Commandments of Good Communication" states that communicators should systematically analyze and clarify their ideas or problems before communicating. This clarification is the first step toward effective communication.
2024:Q44.reference: Textbook Page 353: "1. Seek to clarify your ideas before communicating... This is the first step toward effective communication."

options.content: The last function of the manager
None of the options is correct

2024:Q45.explanation: Because of the concept of the 'Primacy of Planning', planning is considered the primary, or first, function a manager must perform.
2024:Q45.reference: Textbook Page 161: "Planning is the primary management function—the one that precedes and is the basis for the organizing, influencing, and controlling functions."

2024:Q46.questionText: Which of the following is a purely procedural step that could be taken to increase the probability that a committee will be successful?

options.content: specifying the authority of the committee
bringing all members into active participation
keeping the goals of the group flexible

2024:Q46.explanation: Under 'Procedural Steps' for committee success, "The committee's authority should be specified" is explicitly listed. Rephrasing, bringing members into participation, and stimulating thought are 'People-Oriented Guidelines'.
2024:Q46.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 14.

2024:Q47.questionText: Thinking for the future output is known as

options.content: All of the options are correct

2024:Q47.explanation: Developing or setting planning premises involves making assumptions about the future conditions upon which alternative plans will be based. It is essentially thinking about future scenarios.
2024:Q47.reference: Textbook Page 164: Step 3 of the Planning Process involves "Develop premises upon which each alternative is based... a premise is an assumption upon which the alternative is based."

2024:Q48.questionText: What is the major purpose of feedback in the communication process?

options.content: It is used by the source to ensure successful communication.
It can be used to boost the legitimate power of managers.
It provides formal documentation of the communication process.
It helps the source avoid questions from the destination.
It fosters lateral communication in the organization.

2024:Q48.explanation: Feedback is the destination's reaction to a message. The major purpose of gathering this feedback is so the source can determine whether the destination derived the intended meaning, thus ensuring successful communication.
2024:Q48.reference: Textbook Page 350: "Feedback is the destination's reaction to a message. It can be used by the source to ensure successful communication."

2024:Q49.questionText: The person in the interpersonal communication situation who originates and encodes information to be shared with another person is called the
2024:Q49.explanation: In the interpersonal communication process, the source (or source/encoder) is the individual who originates and encodes the information that is to be shared with another person.
2024:Q49.reference: Textbook Page 348: "The source/encoder is the person in the interpersonal communication situation who originates and encodes information to be shared with others."

2024:Q50.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an interest group?

options.content: a group of friends interested in interested in rock music
a group meeting to consider the feasibility of a new product
a group meeting to prepare the monthly financial reports
a group of workers pressing management for better pay

2024:Q50.explanation: An interest group forms because members share a common concern about a specific issue (e.g., pressing management for better pay). A group of friends listening to music is a Friendship Group. The other options are formal Task or Command groups.
2024:Q50.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Based on the definition of Interest Group on Slide 21.

2024:Q51.questionText: What is the core of making a plan?
2024:Q51.explanation: Planning is inherently future-oriented. It involves determining how the organization can get where it wants to go, which requires analyzing foreseen opportunities and thinking in advance.
2024:Q51.reference: Textbook Page 159: "Planning is the process of determining how the organization can get where it wants to go..." which fundamentally requires thinking in advance.

2024:Q52.questionText: Which of the following statements about groupthink is true?

options.content: Groupthink cannot take place in a newly formed group.
A group with high levels of mistrust and conflicts is likely to be most susceptible to groupthink.
A group with a high level of cohesiveness is likely to be susceptible to groupthink.
Managers must help committees to establish groupthink to generate alternative problem solutions.
A group which is highly competitive will most probably result in groupthink.

2024:Q52.explanation: Groupthink occurs when the "desire for agreement so dominates the group that it overrides the need to realistically appraise alternative problem solutions." High cohesiveness creates this strong desire for agreement and conformity, making the group highly susceptible to groupthink.
2024:Q52.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Inferred from the definition and symptoms of Groupthink on Slide 16.

2024:Q53.questionText: At what stage of the planning becomes the most feasible plan that can be implemented.
2024:Q53.explanation: After evaluating options, the manager chooses the best (most feasible) alternative to reach the objectives, which is then developed into actionable plans.
2024:Q53.reference: Textbook Page 164: Step 4 of the Planning Process is "Choose best alternative for reaching objectives."

2024:Q54.questionText: ____ is the process of sharing information with other individuals.
2024:Q54.explanation: Communication is explicitly defined in the textbook as the process of sharing information with other individuals.
2024:Q54.reference: Textbook Page 348: "Communication is the process of sharing information with other individuals."

2024:Q55.questionText: Planning establishes a ground standard for
2024:Q55.explanation: Planning establishes the objectives and standards that the Controlling function then uses to measure actual performance against to determine if goals are being met.
2024:Q55.reference: Textbook Page 161 (and referenced in Control chapters): Planning is the basis for controlling, as controlling compares performance against the standards set during planning.

2024:Q56.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of division of labor?

options.content: It results in easier and more efficient work.
It broadens the scope of work.
It emphasizes the human variable in organizations.
It results in high levels of employee motivation.

2024:Q56.explanation: An explicit advantage of division of labor is that when workers concentrate on performing only one job, they naturally try to make the job easier and more efficient.
2024:Q56.reference: Textbook Page 253: "Second, workers who concentrate on performing only one job naturally try to make the job easier and more efficient."

2024:Q57.explanation: In the context of the planning process, developing premises means formulating assumptions about future conditions and environments upon which alternative plans will be based.
2024:Q57.reference: Textbook Page 164: "a premise is an assumption upon which the alternative is based."

2024:Q58.questionText: Which of the following is one of the three main components of the management system that Weber termed a bureaucracy?

options.content: close, personal relations among organization members

2024:Q58.explanation: Weber's bureaucratic model includes three main concepts: detailed procedures and rules, impersonal relationships, and a clearly outlined organizational hierarchy.
2024:Q58.reference: Textbook Page 252: "Bureaucracy is the term Max Weber used to describe a management system that includes three primary components: detailed procedures and rules, a clearly outlined organizational hierarchy, and impersonal relationships among organization members."

2024:Q59.questionText: An individual's emotional intelligence is characterized by self-awareness, self-motivation, self-regulation, empathy for others, and
2024:Q59.explanation: According to Daniel Goleman's concept of emotional intelligence, it is characterized by five key traits: self-awareness, self-motivation, self-regulation, empathy for others, and adeptness in building relationships.
2024:Q59.reference: Textbook Page 347: "Goleman characterizes an individual's emotional intelligence as being characterized by self-awareness, self-motivation, self-regulation, empathy for others, and adeptness in building relationships."

2024:Q60.questionText: ____ is the mode of thinking that group members engage in when the desire for agreement so dominates the group that it overrides the need to realistically appraise alternative problem solutions.
2024:Q60.explanation: This is the exact definition of Groupthink provided in the lecture.
2024:Q60.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found verbatim on Slide 16.

2024:Q61.questionText: ____ resources refer to the machines used during the manufacturing process.
2024:Q61.explanation: In the breakdown of organizational resources, the textbook explicitly defines 'Capital resources' as the machines or equipment used directly in the manufacturing process to maintain desired production levels.
2024:Q61.reference: Textbook Page 8: "Capital resources are machines used during the manufacturing process. Modern machines, or equipment, can be a major factor in maintaining desired production levels."

2024:Q62.questionText: This role performed by Trot can be called
2024:Q62.context: Trot is the CEO of a consulting firm. He plays a key role in guiding the activities of organization members in appropriate directions.
2024:Q62.explanation: The textbook formally defines influencing as the process of guiding the activities of organization members in appropriate directions. Trot's role perfectly aligns with this definition.
2024:Q62.reference: Textbook Page 346: "Influencing is the process of guiding the activities of organization members in appropriate directions."

2024:Q63.questionText: Organizational communication that does not follow the lines of the organizational chart is specifically called
2024:Q63.explanation: Informal organizational communication is specifically defined as communication that does not follow the formal lines of the organization chart, but rather follows the pattern of personal relationships.
2024:Q63.reference: Textbook Page 355: "Informal organizational communication does not follow the lines of the organization chart."

2024:Q64.questionText: ____ skills are very important to managers at the lower, middle and top levels.
2024:Q64.explanation: According to the classic view of management skills, while the need for technical and conceptual skills varies depending on the management level, 'Human Skills' remain highly and equally important across top, middle, and supervisory levels.
2024:Q64.reference: Textbook Page 11: "Human skills, however, are extremely important to managers at top, middle, and lower (or supervisory) levels. The common denominator of all management levels, after all, is people."

2024:Q65.questionText: This is a fault in the ____ function of management.
2024:Q65.context: Gayle has not established appropriate performance standards for her team.
2024:Q65.explanation: Establishing and utilizing performance standards is a core component of the "Comparing Measured Performance To Standards" step within the controlling process. Failing to establish appropriate standards prevents successful controlling.
2024:Q65.reference: Textbook Page 505: "Comparing Measured Performance to Standards... A standard is the level of activity established to serve as a model for evaluating organizational performance."

2024:Q66.questionText: The more resources unused during the production process, the more ____ the manager.
2024:Q66.explanation: Managerial efficiency deals directly with the proportion of resources contributing to productivity. The textbook explicitly correlates wasted or unused resources with managerial inefficiency.
2024:Q66.reference: Textbook Page 10: "The more resources wasted or unused during the production process, the more inefficient is the manager."

2025:Q1.questionText: Controlling does not highlight the deviations in the process.
2025:Q1.explanation: The entire purpose of control and comparing measured performance to standards is to signal or highlight when deviations from the plan are occurring so that corrective action can be taken.
2025:Q1.reference: Textbook Page 502: "We must develop methods of measurement and control to signal when deviations from the plan are occurring so that corrective action can be taken."

2025:Q2.questionText: Organizing is the process of establishing orderly uses for all resources within the management system.
2025:Q2.explanation: This is the exact, verbatim definition of organizing provided in the textbook.
2025:Q2.reference: Textbook Page 249: "Organizing is the process of establishing orderly uses for all resources within the management system."

2025:Q3.questionText: Vertical dimensioning is directly related to the concept of the scalar relationship that is, the chain of command.
2025:Q3.explanation: Vertical dimensioning encompasses the scalar relationship (chain of command), mapping how authority scales downward from the individual at the top to those at the bottom.
2025:Q3.reference: Textbook Page 260: "Vertical dimensioning refers to the extent to which an organization uses vertical levels to separate job responsibilities. Vertical dimensioning is directly related to the concept of the scalar relationship—that is, the chain of command."

2025:Q4.questionText: Corrective actions are necessary after analyzing the deviations.
2025:Q4.explanation: If the comparison step shows that performance is significantly different from standards (a deviation), the required next step in the controlling process is to take corrective action to bring performance up to the standard.
2025:Q4.reference: Textbook Page 506: "After actual performance has been measured and compared with established performance standards, the next step in the controlling process is to take corrective action if necessary."

2025:Q5.questionText: Human skills, unlike technical skills, involve the ability to see the organization as a whole.
2025:Q5.explanation: The ability to see the organization as a whole is defined as 'Conceptual Skills', whereas 'Human Skills' deal with the ability to work effectively with people.
2025:Q5.reference: Textbook Page 11: "Conceptual skills involve the ability to see the organization as a whole."

2025:Q6.questionText: An organization that wants to retain an employee may need to assist that employee's spouse in his or her career development as well.
2025:Q6.explanation: Although not explicitly outlined in the core text of this chapter, this is a standard external HR management concept regarding dual-career couples and employee retention. Retaining a highly valued employee often requires addressing work-life constraints, including assisting a trailing spouse.
2025:Q6.reference: Standard HR Management principle regarding employee retention and dual-career couples (Not explicitly detailed in the provided textbook chapter).

2025:Q7.questionText: The supply of individuals from which to recruit is continually changing, which means that at times, finding appropriate human resources will be much harder than at other times.
2025:Q7.explanation: The textbook explicitly states that the labor market is dynamic and the supply of individuals to recruit from is continually changing, making finding appropriate human resources harder at certain times.
2025:Q7.reference: Textbook Page 297: "The supply of individuals from which to recruit is continually changing. Thus, there are times when finding appropriate human resources is much harder than at other times."

2025:Q8.questionText: Wikstrom's human resource inventory forms are meant to be used exclusively for filling managerial positions and cannot be used for filling nonmanagerial positions.
2025:Q8.explanation: While Wikstrom's specific examples focus heavily on management personnel, the textbook explicitly notes that similar forms can be used to keep a human resource inventory of nonmanagerial personnel as well.
2025:Q8.reference: Textbook Page 299: "As you can see, Wikstrom’s forms... are focused on management personnel. Of course, similar forms could be used to keep a human resource inventory of nonmanagerial personnel."

2025:Q9.questionText: A task group is a formal group outlined in the chain of command on an organization chart.
2025:Q9.explanation: A group outlined in the chain of command is a 'Command Group', whereas a 'Task Group' is formed for nonroutine tasks.
2025:Q9.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 9.

2025:Q10.questionText: The membership of friendship groups in an organization tend to remain static over long periods of time.
2025:Q10.explanation: Informal groups like friendship groups are not established by management decree and tend to change as personal affiliations, work locations, and employee turnover occur. They are generally dynamic, not static.
2025:Q10.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Inferred from the definition of informal groups on Slide 6 and general management theory.

2025:Q11.questionText: A people-related step in building an effective team is setting stable goals and priorities for the team.
2025:Q11.explanation: Setting goals and priorities is typically considered a procedural or task-oriented step, not a people-oriented guideline. People-oriented guidelines involve rephrasing ideas, ensuring participation, and stimulating thought.
2025:Q11.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 14 (Procedural) vs Slide 15 (People-Oriented).

2025:Q12.questionText: Henri Fayol recommends that businesses establish multiple guiding authorities when organizing resources.
2025:Q12.explanation: Henri Fayol's General Principles of Management explicitly include 'Unity of Command' and 'Unity of Direction'. These principles dictate that employees should receive orders from only one superior and that there should be one head and one unified plan for a group of activities having the same objective. Therefore, establishing multiple guiding authorities contradicts Fayol's framework.
2025:Q12.reference: Chapter 2: History and Current Thinking - Answer found on Slide 13 under General Principles of Management.

2025:Q13.questionText: Span of management refers to the number of organizational levels below that of a particular manager's.
2025:Q13.explanation: Span of management describes how many individuals a manager directly supervises, not the number of organizational levels below them.
2025:Q13.reference: Textbook Page 262: "Span of management—also called span of control, span of authority, span of supervision, and span of responsibility—is the number of individuals a manager supervises."

2025:Q14.questionText: According to the concept of corporate social responsibility, managers should regard societal goals as more important than organizational goals.
2025:Q14.explanation: Corporate social responsibility means protecting and improving both the welfare of society and the interests of the organization simultaneously. It does not state that societal goals are more important, but rather that a manager must strive to achieve societal as well as organizational goals.
2025:Q14.reference: Textbook Page 52: "According to the concept of corporate social responsibility, a manager must strive to achieve societal as well as organizational goals." Slide 9 emphasizes balancing corporate health with stakeholder relations.

2025:Q15.questionText: A programmed decision is typically a one-shot structured decision.
2025:Q15.explanation: A programmed decision is routine and repetitive. A one-shot, unique, or novel decision defines a nonprogrammed decision.
2025:Q15.reference: Textbook Page 182: "A programmed decision is routine and repetitive... In contrast, a nonprogrammed decision is typically a one-shot decision that is usually less structured than programmed decisions."

2025:Q16.questionText: What is the main purpose of the management by exception concept?

options.content: To focus on minor variances for operational improvements.
To minimize management's involvement in all business operations.
To involve management in every decision regarding business direction.
To notify management only of significant variances from planned results.

2025:Q16.explanation: The management by exception concept is a core controlling principle closely tied to the flowchart of the control process. It means a manager should only intervene (take corrective action) when performance is "significantly different from standards" (a significant variance), allowing them to ignore minor variances and focus their time efficiently.
2025:Q16.reference: Textbook Page 504 (Figure 21.2): The controlling subsystem flowchart dictates that action is only taken when "Performance [is] significantly different from standards".

2025:Q17.questionText: Which of the following features is of Formal organization -:

options.content: Directed by company rules and regulations

2025:Q17.explanation: A formal organization refers strictly to the designated relationships and structures explicitly outlined by management, which are directed by official company rules and regulations. While managers are appointed in a formal structure, whether they are actual "leaders" is not a guaranteed feature of the structure itself.
2025:Q17.reference: Textbook Page 256: "Formal structure is defined as the relationships among organizational resources as outlined by management; informal structure is defined as the patterns of relationships that develop because of the informal activities..."

2025:Q18.questionText: Name one of the basic concepts for smoothly running an organisation.

options.content: None of the options is correct

2025:Q18.explanation: Management is the core encompassing concept whose primary role is to smoothly guide the organization towards its goals through the effective use of resources.
2025:Q18.reference: Textbook Page 5: "Essentially, the role of managers is to guide organizations toward goal accomplishment... Management moves an organization toward its purposes or goals by assigning activities organization members perform."

2025:Q19.questionText: Organizing is the process of _____ the activities of an enterprise and _____
2025:Q19.explanation: Organizing essentially involves defining (identifying and dividing work into major tasks) and grouping them (departmentalizing those activities) to establish an orderly use of resources.
2025:Q19.reference: Textbook Page 249-250 (The Organizing Process) and Page 264: Highlights determining major tasks, dividing work, and "Departmentalizing is the process of establishing departments" (grouping activities).

2025:Q20.questionText: At what step of the planning can be processed with the topmost and applicable plan would be implemented
2025:Q20.explanation: Selecting the best alternative (or 'selecting up objective' based on the flawed wording of the option) is the step where the most applicable plan is chosen for implementation.
2025:Q20.reference: Textbook Page 164 (The Planning Process): "Step 4: Choose best alternative for reaching objectives."

2025:Q21.questionText: In HRM, what does the term "training and development" refer to?
2025:Q21.explanation: Training is defined as developing qualities in human resources to make them more productive. Determining training needs involves identifying the information or skill areas of an individual or group that need further development to enhance their knowledge and skills.
2025:Q21.reference: Textbook Page 303: "Training is the process of developing qualities in human resources that will enable them to be more productive..."

2025:Q22.questionText: It is the process of ensuring that events conform to plans.
2025:Q22.explanation: The textbook provides the strict definition of control: "ensuring that an event occurs as it was planned to occur." Controlling is the process managers go through to do this.
2025:Q22.reference: Textbook Page 502: "Stated simply, control entails ensuring that an event occurs as it was planned to occur... Controlling is the process managers go through to control."

options.content: Framework within which managerial and operating tasks are performed

2025:Q23.explanation: Structure is the designated relationships among all resources of the management system, facilitating the use of each resource individually and collectively. This encompasses the framework for both the managerial hierarchy and the operating tasks performed by employees.
2025:Q23.reference: Textbook Page 256: "Structure refers to the designated relationships among resources of the management system. Its purpose is to facilitate the use of each resource..."

2025:Q24.questionText: In which pace of the planning process, two sides of a coin of each alternative are examined.
2025:Q24.explanation: Evaluating alternatives is the step where the pros and cons of different courses of action are analyzed before a final choice is made.
2025:Q24.reference: Textbook Page 164: Evaluating alternatives is the step where managers assess the benefits and drawbacks of each potential course of action.

options.content: The last function of the manager
None of the options is correct

2025:Q25.explanation: Due to the concept of Primacy of Planning, it is the foundational and primary function that precedes organizing, influencing, and controlling.
2025:Q25.reference: Textbook Page 161: "Planning is the primary management function—the one that precedes and is the basis for the organizing, influencing, and controlling functions."

2025:Q26.questionText: The controlling function is performed by
2025:Q26.explanation: Based on the overarching principles of management, all levels of management—top-level, middle-level, and lower-level (first-line) management—execute the controlling function. For instance, top managers control total company plans, middle managers control operations, and first-line managers control specific activities.
2025:Q26.reference: Textbook Page 516 (Figure 21.6) outlines how different management levels (Top, Middle, First-line) all use information systems to support control within their specific organizational levels.

2025:Q27.questionText: Thinking for the future output is known as

options.content: All of the options are correct

2025:Q27.explanation: Developing or setting planning premises involves making assumptions and forecasts about future conditions that will affect the execution of the plans.
2025:Q27.reference: Textbook Page 164: Step 3 of the Planning Process involves "Develop premises upon which each alternative is based... a premise is an assumption upon which the alternative is based."

2025:Q28.questionText: What is the point of distinction between formal and informal organization

options.content: The managers are the leaders in case of formal organization while in case of informal organization the managers may or may not be the leaders and the leaders are chosen by the groups
Formal organization is flexible in nature while informal is rigid in nature

2025:Q28.explanation: Formal structures are outlined explicitly by management, placing appointed managers as the structural heads. Informal structures develop organically from informal activities, meaning leaders emerge naturally from the group. Option B is incorrect as formal structures tend to be more rigid than informal ones.
2025:Q28.reference: Textbook Page 256: "Formal structure is defined as the relationships among organizational resources as outlined by management; informal structure is defined as the patterns of relationships that develop because of the informal activities..."

2025:Q29.questionText: ______ is the management function through which managers compare present performance to preestablished performance standards.
2025:Q29.explanation: Controlling is the process of comparing actual performance to predetermined standards to see if performance aligns and taking remedial action if needed.
2025:Q29.reference: Textbook Page 502: "According to Roberto Mockler, controlling is a systematic effort by business management to compare performance to predetermined standards..."

2025:Q30.questionText: In the context of the personnel function, what is the significance of job analysis?
2025:Q30.explanation: Job analysis is a technique used to gain an understanding of what a job entails (resulting in a job description) and what kind of person should be hired (resulting in a job specification). In essence, it defines the job roles and responsibilities.
2025:Q30.reference: Textbook Page 298: "Job analysis is a technique commonly used to gain an understanding of what a task entails and the type of individual who should be hired to perform that task."

2025:Q31.questionText: Controlling function brings the management cycle back to the
2025:Q31.explanation: Controlling involves checking performance against plans. If corrective action is needed, the process flows back to "change plans, organization, or influencing methods." Because planning and control are "inseparable functions" (Siamese twins), controlling naturally feeds directly back into planning to adjust future standards or plans.
2025:Q31.reference: Textbook Page 502 ("planning and control are virtually inseparable functions") and Page 504 Figure 21.2 ("Take corrective action: change plans...").

2025:Q32.questionText: Looking after the change in an organizational environment doesn't come with any surprises. Address importance of planning related to the topic:

options.content: Planning reduces the risk of uncertainties

2025:Q32.explanation: The protective purpose of planning is specifically designed to minimize risk by reducing uncertainties surrounding business conditions, thereby preventing surprises in a changing environment.
2025:Q32.reference: Textbook Page 160: "The protective purpose of planning is to minimize risk by reducing the uncertainties surrounding business conditions..."

2025:Q33.questionText: Which HRM function is responsible for recruiting and selecting employees?
2025:Q33.explanation: The process of recruiting and selecting employees falls directly under the 'Providing Human Resources' function of HRM, which encompasses Step 1: Recruitment and Step 2: Selection.
2025:Q33.reference: Textbook Page 296 (Figure 13.1): Displays 'Recruitment' and 'Selection' as the first two steps in providing appropriate human resources.

2025:Q34.questionText: Which one is a type of Organizational structures
2025:Q34.explanation: Functional structure (departmentalization based on function) is a primary type of organizational structure outlined in the textbook, alongside product, geographic, customer, and matrix structures.
2025:Q34.reference: Textbook Page 264: "Departments Based on Function: The most widely used basis for establishing departments..."

2025:Q35.questionText: Which of the following statements does not highlight the relationship between planning and controlling

options.content: Planning and controlling are separable twins of management.
Planning without controlling is meaningless; controlling without planning is blind.
Planning is prescriptive, controlling is evaluative.
Planning and controlling are interrelated and interdependent.

2025:Q35.explanation: The textbook explicitly states that planning and control are "virtually inseparable functions" and calls them the "Siamese twins of management." Therefore, stating they are "separable" is false and does not accurately highlight their true relationship.
2025:Q35.reference: Textbook Page 502: "As implied by this definition, planning and control are virtually inseparable functions. In fact, these two functions have been called the Siamese twins of management."

2025:Q36.questionText: The process of organizing involves following steps A. Identification and division of work, B. Assignment of duties, C. Establishing reporting relationship, D. Departmentalization (Arrange them in correct order)
2025:Q36.explanation: The logical sequence of organizing starts with identifying and dividing the work into manageable tasks (A), grouping those activities into departments (D), assigning specific duties to individuals (B), and finally establishing reporting relationships or a chain of command (C).
2025:Q36.reference: Textbook Page 250 (Figure 11.2): The organizing process flows from determining major tasks to dividing them into subtasks, then allocating resources and directives (grouping, assigning, and establishing scalar relationships).

2025:Q37.questionText: Which of the following would be considered a formal group?

options.content: task force for employee birthday celebrations
bringing people from various functions to solve a business dilemma

2025:Q37.explanation: A group formed by management to solve a business dilemma (a nonroutine task) is a formal "Task Group." Birthday, reading, and bowling groups are informal interest or friendship groups.
2025:Q37.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Based on the definition of Task Group on Slide 9.

2025:Q38.questionText: ______ can be defined as guiding the activities of organization members in appropriate directions.
2025:Q38.explanation: Influencing is explicitly defined in the textbook as the process of guiding the activities of organization members in appropriate directions.
2025:Q38.reference: Textbook Page 346: "Influencing is the process of guiding the activities of organization members in appropriate directions."

2025:Q39.questionText: The information the receiver gets is called
2025:Q39.explanation: The encoded information that the source intends to share and that the receiver (decoder/destination) ultimately gets and interprets is called the message.
2025:Q39.reference: Textbook Page 348: "Encoded information that the source intends to share constitutes a message... This person receives the signal and decodes, or interprets, the message to determine its meaning."

2025:Q40.questionText: Which of the following is not important for controlling function?

options.content: It helps in judging the accuracy of standards.

2025:Q40.explanation: Controlling ensures events occur as planned, which naturally promotes order and alignment with goals. Therefore, "restricting coordination" is false and not an important or intended outcome of the controlling function.
2025:Q40.reference: Textbook Page 502: "control entails ensuring that an event occurs as it was planned to occur."

2025:Q41.questionText: Identify the correct sequence of the steps involved in the controlling process.

options.content: Measurement of actual performance, Taking corrective action, Setting performance standards, Comparison of actual performance with standards, Analysing deviations
Comparison of actual performance with standards, Setting performance standards. Measurement of actual performance, Analysing deviations, Taking corrective action
Setting performance standards, Measurement of actual performance, Comparison of actual performance with standards, Analysing deviations, Taking corrective action
Taking corrective action, Measurement of actual performance, Comparison of actual performance with standards, Analysing deviations, Setting performance standards

2025:Q41.explanation: First, performance standards must be set. Then, the formal controlling process steps follow: 1. Measuring performance, 2. Comparing measured performance to standards (which highlights and analyzes deviations), and 3. Taking corrective action. Option 'c' perfectly outlines this logical progression.
2025:Q41.reference: Textbook Page 503: "there are three main steps in the controlling process: 1. Measuring performance 2. Comparing measured performance to standards 3. Taking corrective action". Page 505 adds: "...before they can take such a measurement, they must establish some unit of measure..." and then establish standards.

2025:Q42.questionText: ______ includes determining tasks and groupings of work. It should not be rigid, but adaptable and flexible to meet challenges as circumstances change.
2025:Q42.explanation: Organizing involves establishing tasks and forming departments (groupings of work). Henri Fayol advised that strict adherence to formal structures is not always advisable, highlighting the need for adaptability and flexibility in organizing.
2025:Q42.reference: Textbook Page 261: "Fayol’s Advice on Using Formal Structure: Henri Fayol has indicated that strict adherence to a particular chain of command is not always advisable... organizations should be adaptable and flexible."

2025:Q43.questionText: At what stage of the planning becomes the most feasible plan that can be implemented.
2025:Q43.explanation: Selecting the best alternative is the stage where the most feasible course of action is chosen to be developed into actual implemented plans.
2025:Q43.reference: Textbook Page 164: Step 4 of the Planning Process is "Choose best alternative for reaching objectives."

2025:Q44.questionText: In controlling, reducing the workers, absenteeism in a factory by 20% is an example of
2025:Q44.explanation: A standard is a "level of activity established to serve as a model for evaluating organizational performance." Because "20%" is a specific, numerical metric used to gauge performance, it represents a quantitative standard.
2025:Q44.reference: Textbook Page 505: "A standard is the level of activity established to serve as a model for evaluating organizational performance."

2025:Q45.questionText: Which of the following is a method used in group or organisational training needs assessment?

options.content: Consideration of current and projected changes

2025:Q45.explanation: Methods for determining training needs include 'Looking into the future', which directly aligns with considering current and projected changes within the organization (e.g., planning to buy new equipment).
2025:Q45.reference: Textbook Page 304: "Another way to determine training needs is to look into the future. If management is planning to buy new equipment, expand..."

2025:Q46.questionText: A collection of individuals whose common work experiences result in the development of a system of interpersonal relationships that extend beyond those established by management is a/an
2025:Q46.explanation: This is the exact definition of an Informal Group provided in the lecture.
2025:Q46.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found verbatim on Slide 6.

options.content: The primary function of the manager
The Last function of a manager

2025:Q47.explanation: Planning is the primary foundation upon which organizing, influencing, and controlling are built.
2025:Q47.reference: Textbook Page 161: "Planning is the primary management function—the one that precedes and is the basis for the organizing, influencing, and controlling functions."

2025:Q48.questionText: ______ are work groups established by the organization that have designate work assignments and specific tasks.
2025:Q48.explanation: Formal groups are defined as existing within an organization by virtue of management decree to perform specific tasks. While "task groups" is a subset, "formal groups" is the broader, correct umbrella term for groups established by the organization with designated assignments.
2025:Q48.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 6.

2025:Q49.questionText: Which term refers to the process of evaluating and improving employee performance?
2025:Q49.explanation: Performance Appraisal is explicitly defined in the textbook as the process of reviewing individuals' past productive activity to evaluate the contribution they have made and provide feedback for improvement.
2025:Q49.reference: Textbook Page 308: "Performance appraisal is the process of reviewing individuals’ past productive activity to evaluate the contribution they have made toward attaining management system objectives."

2025:Q50.questionText: Which one of the following is among the steps of Organizing -
2025:Q50.explanation: Organizing involves allocating directives and resources, which encompasses both the assignment of duties to specific roles and the establishment of reporting relationships (the chain of command).
2025:Q50.reference: Textbook Page 250: Step 4 of the organizing process is "Allocate resources and directives for subtasks." This involves assigning duties and establishing the scalar relationship (reporting relationships).

2025:Q51.questionText: Planning establishes a ground standard for
2025:Q51.explanation: Planning sets the objectives and standards that the controlling function later uses to measure actual performance against.
2025:Q51.reference: Textbook Page 161: Planning is the basis for controlling, as controlling compares performance against the standards set during planning.

2025:Q52.questionText: It helps to cross the gap between the current position and the future
2025:Q52.explanation: Planning is defined as determining how the organization can get where it wants to go (future position) from its current position.
2025:Q52.reference: Textbook Page 159: "Planning is the process of determining how the organization can get where it wants to go..."

2025:Q53.questionText: which of the following is an advantage of Functional structure

options.content: Functional structure leads to occupational specialization
Functional structure promotes better control and coordination within the department

2025:Q53.explanation: Departmentalization based on function intrinsically groups people with similar skills, leading to occupational specialization. Additionally, placing power in functional heads promotes consistency, which improves control and coordination within that specific department.
2025:Q53.reference: Textbook Page 265: "The major advantage of functional departmentalization is power of functional heads... consistency... Occupational specialization is another advantage."

2025:Q54.explanation: Basic managerial activities—specifically people-related and task-related skills—encompass supervising (monitoring operations), motivating (which is the core of the 'influencing' function), and stimulating/actuating personnel to reach organizational goals efficiently.
2025:Q54.reference: Textbook Pages 6, 12, 13: Supervising falls under "monitoring operations" (Page 13). Motivating and stimulating (actuating) fall under the "Influencing" function (Page 6).

2025:Q55.questionText: The actual achievements compared with the objectives of the job is
2025:Q55.explanation: Comparing actual productive activity (achievements) against the management system objectives is the process of reviewing Job Performance during a Performance Appraisal.
2025:Q55.reference: Textbook Page 308: Discusses performance appraisal as reviewing past productive activity to evaluate contribution to management system objectives.

2025:Q56.questionText: Which performance appraisal methods consumes a lot of time?
2025:Q56.explanation: While specific appraisal methods like the essay method are not detailed heavily in the provided textbook chapter, in standard HRM theory, the 'Essay method' requires the evaluator to write a detailed, free-form narrative describing the employee's performance. This makes it highly time-consuming compared to checking boxes on Rating Scales.
2025:Q56.reference: Standard HR Management principle (Not explicitly detailed in the provided textbook or slides).

2025:Q57.questionText: Which of the following is a benefit of employee training?

options.content: Helps people identify with organisational goals
Provides a good climate for learning, growth and co - ordination

2025:Q57.explanation: Training is defined as developing qualities in human resources to make them more productive. By utilizing structured techniques for developing skills and transmitting information, training provides a climate for learning, growth, and improved coordination.
2025:Q57.reference: Textbook Page 303: "Training is the process of developing qualities in human resources..." Slides 36-39 cover techniques that facilitate learning and skill development.

2025:Q58.questionText: Which of the following statements about groupthink is true?

options.content: Groupthink cannot take place in a newly formed group.
A group with high levels of mistrust and conflicts is likely to be most susceptible to groupthink.
A group with a high level of cohesiveness is likely to be susceptible to groupthink.
Managers must help committees to establish groupthink to generate alternative problem solutions.
A group which is highly competitive will most probably result in groupthink.

2025:Q58.explanation: Groupthink happens when the desire for agreement dominates the group. A highly cohesive group is naturally more driven by agreement and conformity, making it highly susceptible to groupthink.
2025:Q58.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Inferred from the definition and symptoms of Groupthink on Slide 16.

2025:Q59.questionText: Which of the following statements is true for the management function?

options.content: It reaches goals by working with and through people.
It is a one-time function in an organization.
It is a series of continuing and unrelated activities.
It involves and concentrates on reaching individual goals.
It does not consider the people aspect of organizations.

2025:Q59.explanation: Management is formally defined as the process of reaching organizational goals by working with and through people and other organizational resources.
2025:Q59.reference: Textbook Page 6: "...management is the process of reaching organizational goals by working with and through people and other organizational resources."

2025:Q60.questionText: Which of the following is an error managers make during the planning stage of management?

options.content: not emphasizing coordination of organization members
not exploring enough viable alternatives for reaching objectives
not monitoring progress in carrying out plans
not taking the time to communicate properly with organization members

2025:Q60.explanation: In common errors associated with each function, the mistake of 'not exploring enough viable alternatives for reaching objectives' is a specific error associated with the Planning function. Establishing departments is Organizing, communicating is Influencing, and monitoring is Controlling.
2025:Q60.reference: Textbook Page 164: Evaluating alternatives is a crucial step in the planning process. Failing to explore viable alternatives is a planning error.
